summary: Ten-phase plan written. Phase 1 vendors upstream Operators.lean verbatim but ORPHANED (not in the Cslib.lean barrel) so the tree stays green; Phase 2 renames HasDia to HasDiamond, converting a divergence into an exact fifth duplicate; Phases 3-7 pre-land all 12 rfl _def bridge lemmas per-module smallest-first (LTL, Temporal, Bimodal, Propositional, Modal), each independently green and committable; Phase 8 is the sole red-window atomic-batch step (import Operators, delete 5 duplicate classes, delete the 12 colliding notation declarations, relocate cited design prose, record the latent-trap invariant, run mk_all); Phase 9 renames the AxiomDia identifiers; Phase 10 runs the full 7-step CSLib CI gate. Caveat: the research report's estimate of 4 sites for the AxiomDia rename is wrong -- the measured census is 198 identifier occurrences across 25 files, which is why that rename is isolated into its own late, droppable phase.
decisions_made: Vendor Operators.lean ORPHANED in Phase 1 rather than adding it to the Cslib.lean barrel immediately. Adding it to the barrel puts both declaration sets in one import closure and turns the whole tree red; mk_all is deferred to Phase 8.

Pre-land all 12 _def bridge lemmas in green, per-module, committable phases BEFORE any notation is deleted. Both sides of each rfl already exist today, so this is legal now and it shrinks the unavoidable red window to deletions plus one import.

The HasDia -> HasDiamond rename (Phase 2) deliberately turns the divergence into an exact FIFTH duplicate of upstream's HasDiamond. Phase 8 then deletes five duplicates uniformly. The report framed this as rename-only and did not note the resulting duplicate.

MEASUREMENT CORRECTION: the report's 'AxiomDiaDuality rename, 4 sites, Low impact' is wrong. Measured against the live tree: AxiomDiaDuality 1, AxiomDiaDualityFwd 36, AxiomDiaDualityBack 37, diaDuality 2, diaDualityFwd 61, diaDualityBack 61 = 198 occurrences across 25 files, concentrated in Modal/Metalogic (the largest subtree). Isolated into Phase 9 so it can be excluded without invalidating anything else.

Verification tiers assigned by edit class: local for the orphaned vendor, interface for the rename and the five bridge-lemma phases, full for Phase 8 (the switch), Phase 9 (the rename batch), and Phase 10 (the CI gate). The full gate still runs before task completion regardless.
Phases 8 and 9 are the only phases declared Commit Mode: atomic-batch. All others are per-substep and independently green.

The docstrings on the deleted HasBox and HasDiamond classes carry cited material (ChagrovZakharyaschev1997 section 3.1, Blackburn2001 chapter 1) and are relocated into the Connectives.lean module docstring, not dropped. The latent instance-registration trap is recorded there as a standing invariant.
dead_ends: Do not follow the research report's literal five-step shape, which vendors Operators.lean AND adds it to the barrel in step 1. That combination is red on arrival: duplicate declarations fire as soon as both modules share an import closure, and the 12 notation ambiguities fire as soon as Connectives.lean imports Operators.lean.
Do not attempt to pre-emptively declare upstream-shaped projection notation in the fork's own Cslib.Logic namespace as a staging trick. It creates exactly the same 12 ambiguities and buys nothing.
Do not delete a local notation declaration without its _def bridge lemma already present. Deleting notation with no replacement breaks every use site in that subtree.

continuation_context.zero_debt: No phase requires sorry, an axiom, or a vacuous definition. If a _def bridge lemma stops closing by rfl, that signals instance/constructor drift -- escalate the phase as [BLOCKED] with the goal state rather than weakening the lemma.
continuation_context.constraint: No GitHub or Zulip prose may be authored by an agent. If PR 649's description needs updating, produce a factual scaffolding file under the task directory for a human to adapt.
continuation_context.territory: Wave 1 is parallel-safe by file territory: Phase 1 owns the new Operators.lean; Phase 2 owns Connectives.lean, Axioms.lean, ProofSystem.lean, Modal/Basic.lean, Modal/Semantics/Birelational.lean; Phases 3-6 each own exactly one syntax module. Phase 7 also touches Modal/Basic.lean and is therefore serialised after Phase 2.
